paragraphs: In Croydon, children in care live with carers approved by the council's own service, Foster Croydon, or by independent fostering agencies such as those listed on this page. The council's statement of purpose for 2025-26 says it aims to keep Croydon children with carers in or around the borough unless their needs are better met further away, and that it wants carers from a wide range of backgrounds to reflect the children it looks after.

Foster Croydon recruits for several kinds of fostering: short-term care while plans are made for a child, long-term care until a young person is ready for independence, parent and child placements, and family and friends (connected persons) care. Each carer has a supervising social worker who visits every six weeks, and there is a duty line in office hours and an out-of-hours rota for evenings and weekends. Support groups include a monthly carers' association meeting and a men's group, and new carers can be matched with an experienced carer as a mentor. Carers complete at least 30 hours of training in their first year and 20 hours each year after that.

Croydon publishes a weekly maintenance allowance for each child, from £208 for children aged up to 4 to £309 for 16 and 17 year olds, plus a weekly skills fee for the carer of £325 at the entry level or £450 at the advanced level. Our Croydon allowance page sets out the extras as well.
If you are weighing up fostering in Croydon, talk to the council and to two or three of the agencies below, and compare what each offers in training, support and pay.
